name: Brahmatal Trek

briefItinerary.title: Bhramatal To Bharamatal Top And Descend To Khorurai

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Lohajung
description: You will be picked up from Rishikesh and start the journey to Lohajung. During the journey from Rishikesh to Lohajung, you will go through mountain alleyways that will connect Kumaon hills to Garhwal.

Though it will be a long journey of 9-10 hours but you will enjoy the drive because of the eye-catchy vistas of the mountains. Before reaching Lohajung, you will get an appealing view of Nanda Ghunti's peak.
We will be reaching Lohajung in the evening and then stay at night.

itinerary.title: Lohajung to Bekaltal
description: The trek will begin from Lohajung central market and then move upwards to the upper region of Lohajung. After a short trek, on your left you will see Mandoli village.
After reaching Begum, it will be almost an hour hike which will take you to Bekaltal which is almost frozen at the time of winters. Bekaltal is located at an altitude of 9690ft.

itinerary.title: Bekaltal to Bhramatal
description: We will start the trek early in the morning and you will go through thickets of oak and rhododendrons. After a few hours of trekking the tree line will end and you will enter the meadows.
You will also get an amazing view of Mount Trishul and Mount Nanda Ghunti. We will head towards Bhramatal, from where you will get the majestic views of mountains and valleys.

itinerary.title: Bhramatal to Bharamatal Top and Descend to Khorurai
description: We will start the trek early in the morning and head towards the Bharamatal top which is an uphill climb. The zigzag ascent trail will take you the Bharamatal Lake which will give you a charismatic view of nature at an altitude of 12250 ft.
You will also witness a 180-degree view of the Himalayan range and peaks. Later, we will descent to Khorurai which is located at an altitude of 9150ft.

itinerary.title: Khorurai to Lohajung
description: After having breakfast in the morning, we start the trek from Khorurai to Lohajun which is almost 3km and takes almost 3 to 4 hours. The trail will go through thick forests of oak and rhododendron.

itinerary.title: Lohajung to Rishikesh
description: This will be the last day of your trip and we will be heading back to Rishikesh.
You will be reaching Rishikesh by 10 PM.

inclusions: Transportation : Rishikesh to Lohajung and return
Vegetarian Meals: All Meals as per menu from first day Dinner to last day Breakfast at Basecamp.
Camping charges: Camping and forest permit fees for Indian Nationals
Trekking equipment: High quality tents (living tent– triple sharing, kitchen tent, dinning tent, toilet tent)
Safety equipment: First aid medical kit, oxygen cylinder, stretchers, rope
Mountaineering qualified and experienced Trek leader, Guides, Cook and Support staff
exclusions: Personal clothing (jacket, shoes, winter clothes etc)
Personal trek gears (stick, poncho, headlight etc)
Mules or Porter to carry personal luggage
backpackOffloading: Offload your backpack to a mule or porter to lighten your load during the trek.
Offloading charges range from ₹300 to ₹500 per day per bag.
Ensure your backpack weighs up to 11 kg and is equipped with a waterproof cover.
Suitcases, trolleys, or duffel bags are not allowed.
thingsToCarry: Thermal Inner Wears (Both Upper and Lower)
Government Photo Identity Card (Passport, Aadhaar Card, Driving license or Voter ID)
thingsToCarryNotes: A small hiking bag is used only if the main bag is given to a porter or mule. It is also needed on the final day of the summit climb.
Rental gear like jackets, shoes, trek poles, headlamps, ponchos, and more is available at Sankri basecamp market.

discrepancies: Overview lists Nearest Airport and Railway Station as "Rishikesh"; Rishikesh has no airport, and the pickup line reads "Haridwar/rishikesh".
Things to Carry note refers to "Sankri basecamp market", but this trek's base camp is Lohajung — appears copied from the Kedarkantha brochure.
Key Notes say food is served "(Sankri to Sankri)", but this trek runs Rishikesh–Lohajung — appears copied from the Kedarkantha brochure.
Key Notes mention spikes and gaiters "for the summit climb during the night trek"; this itinerary has no night summit climb.
Trek name is spelled both "Brahmatal" (cover) and "Bhramatal"/"Bharamatal" (itinerary pages).
